data.name: Himavati
data.gender_notes: Himavati is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Himavati is the daughter of Himavan, the king of the Himalayas. The name symbolizes strength, stability, and serenity. The name Himavati carries the meaning “Daughter of the Himalayas” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Himavati usually hope their child will grow to embody daughter of the himalayas and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine femininity and the power of nature.
data.etymology: Himavati belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Daughter of the Himalayas.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Himavati total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Himavati is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and is associated with the majestic Himalayas, the abode of the gods. It is believed that using this name invokes a sense of connection and reverence towards the mountains, representing the power and stability of nature.
data.spiritual_significance: Himavati is considered a sacred name with deep spiritual roots. It is believed that invoking this name can connect the individual to the divine energies of the universe, instilling a sense of serenity, peace, and strength within. In Hindu tradition, it is also believed that the name holds the power to purify the mind and spirit, bringing forth inner peace and harmony.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Himavati is named after the goddess Himavati, symbolizing purity, grace, and the giver of eternal bliss. She is believed to be the embodiment of the snow-capped mountains, inspiring awe and evoking a sense of peace and tranquility.

vedic_reference.root_origin: Sanskrit root हिम (hima) + वती (vatī) = daughter of snow

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Himavati is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the daughter of the king of the Himalayas. The name Himavati carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Himavati is a Hindu goddess and the wife of Shiva.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Himavati remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.
